items.title: Cascadu interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: vowed with Lydia to come back and you know, spend some time with the kids and everything else.

ctx.x: How did you learn the vocal phrases and melodies that I heard yesterday? That sounds like a long, seems like a long-term —

Some of that was from Trinidad tradition. And lot of it is — and it’s all Yoruba, right? So the tradition that, although there is Arara in Trinidad and there are Arara villages etcetera, this particular piece was Yoruba. And Trinidad was actually the patron saint of the island is Shango and the Shango “cult” quote unquote in Trinidad is a complete retention of the Yoruba presence, those divinities for the Africans who arrived in Trinidad. So I grew up with that stuff. My — I didn’t know, but my mother’s family…
Well this goes back to what we were talking about when we started today, this, what is it that that percussion music brings out of you.
